catalog_quote: Le dadjo-Sila distingue cinq timbres vocaliques, dédoublés par une corrélation de longueur. Il oppose deux hauteurs tonales dont le rendement lexical est extrêmement faible (le fonctionnement du sytème tonal, qui pourrait être caractérisé par un ton haut marqué, est encore mal compris). D'un point de vue phonotactique les mots sont souvent longs et peuvent comporter différents groupes consonantiques (ex. kùßùÑdìcé 'écorce', •ìkìdáaÑgè 'descendre', dèktéskè 'dénouer (cheveux)').

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding sentence is verbatim at the stated place (Boyeldieu 2008, sec. 1.2, HAL PDF p.2) in the text we hold/PDF. (2) Deciding source: a 2008 first-hand sketch chapter by the language's only modern describer; not a phonology, and the author flags the tone system as poorly understood and possibly marked-High. sources.quote: Sila (own data, Abeche 1995) is transcribed with H/L tone marks throughout and demonstratives 'directly follow the head noun (with a regressive tone-raising effect): sìttè 'rope' / sìtté án 'this rope'' -- i.e. Sila prosody is treated as tone. For the sister language Shatt Damam (not Sila) the same author writes: 'High pitch does not normally appear more than once in a single word ... it is assigned according to rules which are not fully understood. Finally, it is not yet clear whether this prosodic system should be analyzed as tonal or as a stress system.' No word-stress rule is given for Sil
